title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency Admission Agreements: One Open Agreement per Resident
content:
**Admissions registry rule — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.** A resident may hold successive private-pay admission agreements, one per admission: a readmission after discharge signs a new agreement. Only one agreement of the resident may be open at a time, an open agreement being one that is pending admission, active, under a discharge notice (the notice period) or converted to another payer source. A new agreement is opened only when no other agreement of the resident is still open.

**What the records must show.** The test is made on the system record before the new agreement is opened: the agreements filed under the resident, and the status each one carries. What a caller says about an earlier stay does not replace that record.

| Resident's other agreement on file | May a new agreement be opened? |
|---|---|
| None | Yes |
| Pending admission, active, in the notice period, or converted to another payer source | No |
| Discharged, closed or cancelled only | Yes |

The number of successive agreements a resident may hold over time is not capped; the limit is on how many are open at once.

**Life of an agreement.** An agreement is signed for a tier and starts pending admission. It becomes active when the resident arrives and private-pay billing starts on the admission date, or is cancelled when the planned admission does not take place. An active agreement moves to the notice period when the center issues a written facility-initiated discharge notice, and back to active when that notice is rescinded (balance cured, Medicaid application submitted, or appeal decided for the resident); from the notice period it becomes discharged when the resident leaves on or after the noticed discharge date. An active agreement becomes discharged when the resident leaves on their own choice, dies, or is transferred to hospital with no return; it is converted when another payer source (Medicaid pending, Medicaid, Medicare Part A or hospice room and board) takes over the stay, and active again when that payer source ends or is denied and private-pay billing resumes. A converted agreement with no private balance or deposit left is closed, and a discharged agreement is closed once the final statement is settled, the deposit disposed of and any credit refunded.
